3b9b99b0c50d67fb9fb349e48254025f95648cd6.summary: A Broadcom Symantec protection bulletin reports a new campaign distributing Poco RAT to Spanish-speaking users in Latin America. The report attributes the campaign to the Darkling APT (aka Dark Caracal), which it says is known to use Bandook-based backdoors. Victims receive phishing emails with malicious PDF attachments that redirect them to download .rev files, which lead to malware droppers that install Poco RAT. The payloads give attackers remote control, command execution and system information collection. The bulletin lists detection names for Symantec and Carbon Black products.
